finding.summary: Correction C-2026-0928-01, re-tested: the published reference verifier reported VALID for a receipt whose signing key it never resolved, so any key naming any issuer passed.

claim.statement: interceptor.py (sha256 d908b9e7...) returns VALID only for receipts whose key resolves to the named issuer, and never INVALID merely because resolution failed.
claim.scope: The 17 core conformance cases; not the interop cases.

test.method_id: signed-receipts/v1 conformance, 17 core cases, resolution only via each case's did_documents
declared_failure_modes: Covers only the 17 core cases; a fault outside them passes.
The pre-fix code has no three-valued result; its bool is mapped VALID/INVALID and it is driven integrity-only when a DID is absent from the fixture map, as deployed.

negative_control.description: The kit's published results for the pre-fix verifier (example-fail-results.json) are scored against vectors.json by this script's comparator; it must report mismatches. It reported 4 of 17.

result.reason: 4 of 17 cases differ from expected: valid-jcs-edge INVALID (expected VALID); unresolvable-key VALID (expected UNVERIFIABLE_KEY); unresolvable-key-forgery VALID (expected UNVERIFIABLE_KEY); unresolvable-key-unsupported-method VALID (expected UNVERIFIABLE_KEY)

remediation.reference: commits 1ae2025fd, acff54074; CORRECTED - reference verifier returns UNVERIFIABLE_KEY, never VALID, for an unresolvable key; served and Hugging Face c

limits: This re-test ran the pre-fix bytes supplied from the issuer's git history at the digest the ledger cites; the public copy the ledger names answered 401, so a stranger cannot fetch these bytes today.
It says nothing about receipts issued with the verifier, only about how the verifier classified the vectors.
